# Pulse

> Pulse measures whether a product catalogue can answer the questions shoppers ask,
> then ranks the missing product data by how many shoppers need it rather than by how
> empty the field is. Run by Resolve Labs. The first audit is free: one category
> export, no account, findings back in 48 hours.

Key facts, each reproducible from the catalogue named beside it:

- On a 216-product laptop shelf, 94 products remain indistinguishable after every
  question a shopper can answer. The catalogue, not the shopper, is the larger gap.
- Ranking a repair by how empty a field is inverts the correct order. Processor is
  missing on 162 of 216 products and ranks last by decision value; screen size is
  missing on 80 and ranks first.
- 161 of 216 missing screen-size values were recoverable from the merchant's own
  product titles before anyone recorded anything new.
- On a 2,176-product catalogue, 52.6% of recorded attribute values duplicate what the
  product photograph already shows. The average product carries 0.90 facts a shopper
  cannot get by looking.
- Pulse has no customers to name and no measured conversion result. It has run no live
  experiment and does not quote an uplift figure.

## Products

- [Decision Audit](https://thepulseapi.com/product/decision-audit): a ranked list of
  which missing product data to record first, from one category export.
- [Decision Verification](https://thepulseapi.com/product/decision-verification):
  re-measure the repaired catalogue and see what moved.
- [Decision Monitor](https://thepulseapi.com/product/decision-monitor): re-measure on a
  schedule and get told when a shelf slips, with the cause.
